text:
chief complaint: sore throat for four days with fever, chills, and difficulty swallowing.
history of present illness: the patient reports four days of sore throat, one night of sweating and chills suspected to be fever, and painful swallowing that limits eating but not drinking cold water. Rapid COVID test negative. Patient has hypertension and type 2 diabetes with home readings that are variable.
physical examination: low-grade temperature of about 100.4°F, blood pressure about 132/80, heart rate 84. Facial sinuses nontender. Nasal turbinates edematous and erythematous with clear discharge. Bilateral peritonsillar erythema and edema with exudates, uvula midline. Right-sided cervical lymphadenopathy. Coarse rhonchi at lung bases that clear with cough. Regular heart rhythm without murmur or rub.
symptoms experienced by the patient: sore throat, fever, chills, sweating, painful swallowing, mild nasal stuffiness, swollen tonsils.
new medications prescribed or changed, including dosages: amoxicillin 500 mg three times daily for 10 days if rapid strep test positive; lidocaine swish and swallow (dosage N/A); ibuprofen as needed (dosage N/A); lisinopril increased from 20 mg to 40 mg once daily.
follow-up instructions: rapid strep test today; lipid panel and hemoglobin A1c ordered; continue hydration; doctor will follow up with results.
